text.content:
Geo-Political notes for Etesia

Wolfsgarde

The City State of Wolfsgarde sits on the eastern banks of the Stone
River, and on the shores of the Gulf of Storms. Wolfsgarde is a key trade
hub. Politically, the stance of Wolfsgarde is commerce and order comes
first, with a generally libertarian and hands off approach. Most things
go as long as they are in line with the common law and consensual in
nature. No particular restrictions on weapons or magic items, however
use/misuse of them inside the city borders may be met with strict
sanction. Deceptive or illusionary magic is particularly disliked in the
course of trade. There are plenty of street performers and such that
incorporate illusion magic in their acts. The City State provides
services to merchants, such as Zone of Truth for negotiations and
contracts. Contracts, warehousing, escrow services, trusted agents,
arbitration, and similar are key industries to the City State.

Due to the wealth and nature of business, Wolfsgarde maintains a robust
force to defend its borders and maintain its independence, of both
conventional and magical means.

Wolfsgarde maintains cordial, if cool, relations with the Shining Star
Protectorate. The relations are strained due to ideological differences,
and the historical attempts of the Protectorate to conquer or otherwise
annex Wolfsgarde into its territory.

The population of Wolfsgarde is cosmopolitan and emissaries of the
surrounding powers and members of all races may be found inside its
borders.

The Shining Star Protectorate (SSP)

The The Shining Star Protectorate, sometimes referred to as “The
Protectorate”, abbreviated as the SSP is characterized by its
ideological bent, perhaps even a hatred, of magical items, things, and
spells. Magic items are generally forbidden in SSP lands. Wealthy, high
ranking, or nobles of the SSP have dispensation to carry or use magical
things.

The citizens of the SSP generally also dislike magic items/users, and
this has resulted in some unfortunate (and gruesome) deaths of magic
users that were discovered or failed to properly hide their abilities by
various mobs of angry citizens.

Due to the anti-magic stance of the SSP, they value hand created items
and clever design. They are known for a high level of craftsmanship and
mechanical contrivances.

The SSP imports materials from Wolfsgarde and Kergrin primarily, but also
seeks out rarer items from Castlemarch and lands beyond.

Despite their public anti-magic stance, the SSP has a strong clergy who
has been known to assist their armies in battle and perform healing for
the populace. The clergy has a strong influence in the governance of the
SSP, whose leaders are known as “The Father” and/or “The Mother.”
Discipline in the SSP society is very strict for public misbehavior.

The SSP has two major towns/cities, Thornshire and Stone Crossing.
Thornshire sits across Wolfsgarde along the Stone River. Ferry service
connects Wolfsgarde and Thornshire. Wolfsgarde forces destroyed, and will
destroy any bridges to limit and prevent incursions across the river.

Stone Crossing to the north sits at a favorable bend in the Big Stone
River. Stone Crossing has ferry service to the other bank, connecting it
to the pre-cataclysm trade route/road.

Stone Crossing also serves as a supply base for the SSP forces
attempting to control (and expand) their western frontier. It is thought
that the SSP also has designs upon bringing Kergrin into its fold at
some point.

SSP is comprised of primarily humans with, some dwarven, gnomish, and
hafling populations who share the anti-magic views of the SSP. Other
races are seen as magical aberrations and are not generally welcome,
unless they are part of high level delegations from other City States,
in which case they are tolerated by the SSP as a matter of necessity.

Kergrin

The City State of Kergrin is located in a pass between the impassible
Bone Mountains. Kergrin serves as the industrial base for numerous mines
and expeditions in the Bone Mountains searching for ores, gems, and
other mineral resources. Kergrin controls access from the west,
defending the southern portions of Etesia from incursion from the North.

Kergrin is comprised mostly of Dwarves, but other races are generally
welcome. Those that prove their worth and value to the City State earn
their welcome. Kergrin has strict rules on the importation of magical
items, requiring a grant from the City State for outsiders to possess
such items. Outsiders found with unapproved items may have them seized
by the City State.

Due to its strategic location, Kergrin maintains strong forces. They
also keep a weather eye to the south, noting the expansionist tendencies
of the SSP.

Yemthas

Yemthas is primarily an Elven kingdom, with pockets of other races
living inside it. Magic is welcomed and embraced, however it is
generally restricted for outsiders. The kingdom is very insular, and
does not tolerate foreigners. Trade with Yemthas is done primarily in
the city of Yemthas. Foreigners found in other parts of the kingdom
without kingdom approval have been known to be executed.

Castlemarch

Castlemarch sits on the isthmus between Etesia and Arniea. Controlling
access, the city state has alternated between trading hub and firebreak
holding back attacking waves from Arniean peoples. With ready access to
the nomadic traders of Arniea, and the resources of the west, many
exotic things can be found in Castlemarch. Castlemarch is home to a high
level of artisans, who build all manner of things.

Given its positions, Castlemarch is known to hire the best warriors to
serve with its army.

Other notes:

The Bone Mountains traverse Etesia from east to west. They are generally
impassible.

Rivers

Rivers depicted on the map are major rivers, and are not readily
fordable and will require a ferry or bridge.

Bridges are Red on the map; Ferries are Blue on the map.

Rivers are used for commerce by floating barges down from the headwaters
to the sea. The river currents are typically 4-6 knots, limiting
upstream traffic.

The North and the Wilds

The Northern reaches of Etesia are not well connected to the rest of the
continent, and are populated by orcs, goblins, and other tribes,
creatures, and monsters.

The wilderness between cities are known to be populated with a variety
of animals, bandits, orcs, goblins, and other monsters.

Depicted on the map are the approximate zones of control of the various
city states. Control exercised by the city states is stronger closer to
town, and weaker / less effective the further away from the center of
power.

Distance

Tile distance on the map represents approximately 75 miles

Terrain

Terrain depicted on the map is general, and not specific to any or all
types of terrain that may be encountered on any given hex.

The Thieves’ Guild

The Thieves Guild is not a singular entity. Each country / populated
area has their own Guild (and perhaps multiple Guilds) that operate in
that territory. These Guilds will vary in nature and composition,
depending on the local politics. In a strong country, they may operate
much like the mob or organized crime, sometimes operating in concert
with the legitimate power, providing opportunity for clandestine
activities, desired smuggling (even if illegal), and other such
shenanigans. In less organized places, they may range from merely a
loose association of criminals to having infiltrated and functionally
dominated the local government (e.g. like the cartels).
